# groundlens

> Geometric LLM hallucination detection. No second LLM. Deterministic. Auditable.

groundlens detects LLM hallucinations using embedding geometry instead of a second LLM. It computes deterministic, auditable scores from the spatial relationships between questions, responses, and source context in embedding space.

## What groundlens does

- SGI (Semantic Grounding Index): detects Type I hallucinations (unfaithfulness) by measuring whether a response engaged with provided context or defaulted to the question.
- DGI (Directional Grounding Index): detects Type II hallucinations (confabulation) by checking whether the question-to-response displacement aligns with a learned grounded direction.
- Type III hallucinations (within-frame factual errors) are undetectable by embedding geometry — this is a fundamental limitation of the distributional hypothesis, not a tool limitation.

## Key properties

- Deterministic: same inputs, same score, every time.
- Sub-second: uses a sentence-transformer model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), not LLM generation.
- Auditable: every score traces to Euclidean distances and cosine similarities.
- Domain calibration: generic AUROC ~0.8, domain-specific reaches 0.90–0.99.

Javier Marin — [jmarin.info](https://jmarin.info)
